messages:
sam: heads-up — ran tonight's perf diff after lowering kernel_selector.selection_threshold from 0.6 -> 0.45. On mixtral-8x7b we get ~+3.8% throughput but some eval regressions on the longform QA set (hallucination + token mismatch). Logs below, attaching quick repro steps.

```
kernel_selector.commit: 9f8a2a
selection_threshold: 0.45
model: mixtral-8x7b
seq_len: 1024
selected_kernel: tiled_attention_v3
previous_kernel: tiled_attention_v2
perf: throughput +3.8%, p50 latency -2.4%
eval_delta: rouge-l -0.7, exact_match -1.9
repro: ./bin/infer --model mixtral-8x7b --kernel tiled_attention_v3 --seq 1024 --prompt-file samples/longform.jsonl
```

anya: ugh. did we also change any rope/head-scaling assumptions in the selector? i remember a recent change that split "head_scale" into per-head config for qwen variants.

liam: i can bisect. i'll run a quick local with forcing kernel=v2 vs v3 to confirm quality delta. if forcing v2 removes the regression it's definitely selector-related.

maria: hold the canary rollout for the mixtral pool until we confirm. we should not push the selector change org-wide until we have a root cause. please paste eval ids for the failing runs.

ci-bot: DeployBot: canary rollout started by sam -> mixtral-pool (target 10%) at 2024-06-10T03:14:00Z. Status: PARTIAL.

sam: repro notes: forcing tiled_attention_v2 restores baseline quality. i dug into the logs and saw inconsistent "rope_scale" values emitted by the runtime before kernel selection: sometimes a scalar, sometimes an array per head. v3 assumes uniform scalar. snippet: 

```diff
- rope_scale = base_scale * global_mult
+ rope_scale = base_scale * (per_head_mult[head_idx] if per_head_mult else global_mult)
```

sam: hypothesis: tiled_attention_v3 merged some KV layout optimizations and expects uniform rope scaling; when the model metadata emits per-head multipliers (recent mixtral build) v3 applies the wrong phase rotation -> attention phase misalignment -> hallucination/regression.

anya: that matches what i saw on qwen-34b earlier when we toggled per-head vs global rope. kernel fast-paths that vectorize over heads can silently break when head-dim/kv-head-dim != expected. we should add a selector guard: prefer v2 if model.metadata.head_scale.is_per_head == true.

liam: i'll run a bisect between commits 9f7b3c -> 9f8a2a and run the nightly eval harness with forced quantization modes (q4_0, q4_1). note: when we toggled quantization earlier, q4_0 vs q4_1 changed angle rounding and made some rotary-op outputs drift; i want to rule out quant as a confounder.

maria: file an incident? set severity P2 for now. add the eval IDs and link to the canary job. ops: please roll back canary until fix is in.

sam: action items: 
- liam: rollback selector change on canary (revert to commit 9f7b3c) and run bisect results in a thread (ETA 45m).
- anya: run per-model unit evals focusing on per-head rope metadata and head_dim vs kv_dim mismatches (ETA 1h).
- sam: add runtime guard in kernel_selector to detect per_head rope_scale and force fallback to tiled_attention_v2 until patched (PR draft opened).

liam: ok starting rollback now. will also run q4_0/q4_1 toggles and upload eval logs.

maria: thanks — once we have bisect/eval logs, i'll coordinate rollback docs and update the incident tracker. ping me when eval IDs are uploaded.

sam: quick note: patch candidate in my branch fixes compute_rope_scaling to respect per-head multipliers and adds a runtime predicate: if per_head multipliers present -> select v2 or v3+compat shim. will open PR after liam confirms bisect.

anya: rough mitigation sounds good. long term we should add a model-metadata contract test so kernel_selector refuses to pick kernels that don't advertise compatible rope/head semantics.

liam: uploaded eval artifacts -> https://ci.redwood/test-runs/98321 (canary v3), https://ci.redwood/test-runs/98322 (forced v2). diff tool shows attention weight phase shift at head indices 3,7,12.

maria: got the links, filing incident now. thanks team. :thumbsup:

sam: final: rolling back selector change on canary + pausing wide rollout. will follow up with PR + unit tests.
